research_question: Can alternative optimal transport costs improve non-rigid shape correspondence?

papers.title: Deep Shells: Unsupervised Shape Correspondence with Optimal Transport
Integrating Efficient Optimal Transport and Functional Maps For Unsupervised Shape Correspondence Learning

findings.statement: Entropy-regularized OT energy integrating squared product-embedding distance enables differentiable Sinkhorn-based shape matching.
findings.evidence: Eq. 8: OT energy integrating squared embedding distance under pi minus entropy regularization enables differentiable Sinkhorn optimization

findings.statement: Pairwise OT ground cost is explicitly encoded as Gibbs density from negative scaled squared embedding distance.
findings.evidence: Eq. 10 defines p_lambda as exponential of negative scaled squared distance for Sinkhorn input

findings.statement: A second OT energy using learned feature distance computes initial soft correspondences, exemplifying an alternative ground cost.
findings.evidence: Eq. 13: OT energy using learned feature distance to compute initial pi, showing alternative ground cost in same pipeline

findings.statement: Product-space embedding of intrinsic eigenfunctions and extrinsic coordinates/normals defines the space where Euclidean distance serves as OT ground cost.
findings.evidence: Eq. 3 embeds shape X into R^{K+6} using intrinsic eigenfunctions plus extrinsic smoothed coordinates and normals whose Euclidean distance becomes ground cost

findings.statement: Sliced Wasserstein distance defined as expectation of 1D Wasserstein distances over random projections provides an O(n log n) time, O(n) memory valid OT metric alternative to O(m^3 log m) Wasserstein and O(m^2) entropic OT.
findings.evidence: Equation 4 defines sliced Wasserstein as expectation over projections with O(n log n)/O(n) valid metric; Equations 2-3 define baseline cubic Wasserstein and quadratic-memory non-metric entropic OT

findings.statement: Energy-based sliced Wasserstein weights slicing directions by an energy function, providing a more discriminative sliced OT variant than uniform slicing.
findings.evidence: Equation 6 defines energy-based sliced Wasserstein expectation under energy-weighted slicing distribution as more discriminative variant; Equation 7 gives importance-sampling estimator

findings.statement: Bidirectional sliced Wasserstein loss aligns Fx vs permuted Fy in both directions for cycle consistency, and its energy-based variant uses a shared slicing distribution with importance weights.
findings.evidence: Equation 10 defines bidirectional SW discrepancy between Fx vs permuted Fy and vice versa; Equation 11 defines bidirectional EBSW with shared slicing distribution

findings.statement: Adaptive test-time refinement via iterated Sinkhorn projections yields an entropic OT plan to improve final point maps, but is restricted to a single inference step due to quadratic memory cost.
findings.evidence: Equation 14 defines iterated Sinkhorn refinement to obtain entropic OT plan with claim of improvement but inference-only use; Equation 3 notes entropic OT still O(m^2) memory and not a valid metric

findings.statement: Ablation on SHREC19 (trained on FAUST+SCAPE) shows replacing BiSW/EBSW with MSE drastically degrades accuracy and removing entropic adaptive refinement increases mean geodesic error from 4.7 to 7.2, directly attributing gains to alternative OT costs.
findings.evidence: Table 4 ablation over OT loss variants (MSE vs BiSW/EBSW) and adaptive refinement; claim-3 states replacing LOT with MSE degrades drastically and removing refinement degrades 4.7 to 7.2

connections.reason: f1 established entropy-regularized OT with Sinkhorn (Eq.8) as differentiable matching energy; new[0] proposes sliced Wasserstein as O(n log n) valid-metric alternative to the O(m^2) non-metric entropic OT noted in eq-3

f3 showed alternative ground cost via learned feature distance OT energy (Eq.13 deep-shells); new[2] extends this to bidirectional sliced/energy-based Wasserstein losses on feature distributions with shared slicing distribution
Both use entropic-regularized OT with KL constraint and Sinkhorn solver; new paper reuses it specifically as iterated Sinkhorn refinement at inference due to quadratic memory

f4 defines ground cost as Euclidean distance in product-space embedding R^{K+6} (eigenfunctions+extrinsic); new[2] assumes ground cost is expectation over 1D Wasserstein distances of projected feature distributions, not Euclidean embedding distance
Table 4 / claim-3 ablation showing BiSW/EBSW outperform MSE validates that bidirectional sliced OT losses improve correspondence

contributions.what_it_adds: Establishes entropy-regularized OT formulation with squared product-embedding ground cost encoded as Gibbs density, plus a second OT energy using learned-feature distance, providing baseline OT costs against which alternatives can be tested.
contributions.stance_toward_prior: orthogonal - first paper in project with no prior findings to support or challenge; establishes foundational OT cost formulation for shape correspondence.
contributions.overlap_with_direction: Partial overlap: paper defines the core squared embedding-distance OT cost and instantiates one alternative ground cost (learned feature distance for initialization in Eq-13 vs geometric embedding distance in Eq-8), but does not systematically compare whether alternative costs improve correspondence.

contributions.what_it_adds: Introduces efficient valid-metric alternative OT costs (uniform sliced Wasserstein and energy-weighted EBSW with Monte Carlo/importance-sampling estimators), implements them as bidirectional feature-alignment losses plus inference-only entropic Sinkhorn refinement, and provides first causal ablation isolating OT cost choice (BiSW/EBSW vs MSE) on SHREC19 and SOTA results on near-isometric (FAUST/SCAPE/SHREC19) and non-isometric (SMAL/DT4D-H) benchmarks.
contributions.stance_toward_prior: Extends and qualifies prior deep-shells entropy-regularized OT framework (f1-f4): confirms alternative ground costs improve matching but replaces training-time entropic OT with linearithmic sliced metrics due to O(m^2) memory and non-metric limitations, relegating entropic OT to post-hoc refinement.
contributions.overlap_with_direction: Direct and central - the paper is explicitly designed to test whether alternative OT costs improve non-rigid correspondence via SW/EBSW vs MSE and refinement ablations, directly answering the research question.
new_open_questions: Whether discriminative gain of EBSW over uniform SW persists beyond single SHREC19 ablation (FAUST+SCAPE training) and on non-isometric SMAL/DT4D-H
Whether O(n log n) theoretical efficiency translates to measured training/inference speedups given L Monte Carlo projections vs Sinkhorn quadratic cost
How to disentangle OT cost improvement from joint FM solver, proper losses and DiffusionNet backbone in total unsupervised loss Eq.13

open_questions.text: Do alternative OT ground costs beyond squared embedding distance and learned-feature initialization distance improve correspondence quality rather than just alignment tightness?
How do entropy regularization and Gibbs scaling affect correspondence accuracy under different ground costs?
Can learned-feature OT cost replace geometric embedding OT cost throughout alignment, not just for initialization?
Does the 4.7 to 7.2 degradation without adaptive refinement and the MSE vs BiSW/EBSW gap generalize beyond SHREC19 to SMAL and DT4D-H non-isometric sets?
What is the sensitivity of correspondence accuracy to number of Monte Carlo projections L and importance-sampling stability for bidirectional EBSW with shared distribution?
Can sliced OT losses alone achieve gains without the functional map solver and proper loss weighting in Eq.13, isolating the OT cost effect from the full pipeline?

novelty_risks.direction: Compare alternative OT ground costs (geometric embedding distance vs learned feature distance) to improve non-rigid correspondence
novelty_risks.note: Paper already defines both costs and uses them in the same pipeline (matching vs initialization), so claiming this comparison as entirely novel would overlap.

novelty_risks.direction: Introduce entropy-regularized OT with Gibbs pairwise cost for unsupervised shape matching
novelty_risks.note: Core formulation already established in this paper, so re-proposing it risks duplication.

novelty_risks.direction: Proposing alternative OT costs for non-rigid shape correspondence using sliced or entropy-regularized variants
novelty_risks.note: Deep-shells already established entropy-regularized OT and learned-feature alternative ground cost (f1-f3), and eot-maps now covers efficient valid-metric slice of alternatives (SW/EBSW + entropic refinement) with direct ablation Table 4 MSE vs BiSW/EBSW, reducing novelty of further OT variant without new theoretical efficiency or metric property.

novelty_risks.direction: Claiming SOTA improvement on FAUST/SCAPE/SHREC19 via joint FM+OT+proper loss pipeline
novelty_risks.note: SOTA claims on FAUST/SCAPE/SHREC19 and SMAL/DT4D-H conflate alternative OT costs with FM solver, DiffusionNet features, and proper losses (eq-13); only isolated OT-cost ablation is Table 4 limited to SHREC19 after FAUST+SCAPE training, risking overlap for future OT-cost-only claims.
